brief: Boston Partners' October portfolio review: U.S. equities diverged sharply. The cap-weighted S&P 500 fell 0.87% while the equal-weighted version gained 5.00%, the widest equal-weight edge since April 2009; the Nasdaq 100 dropped 6.63% on doubts about monetizing AI buildout spending, dragging the Magnificent Seven down 4.67% versus the S&P 493's 1.34% gain. Investors rotated into bonds (Agg +2.44%, best since Dec 2023) and defensives (Staples, Utilities, Health Care); Communication Services was the worst sector as Alphabet's and Meta's AI capital spending showed no revenue payoff, the two stocks causing 94% of the sector's loss. Energy led on an oil spike (WTI to $104.12, Brent to $111.73) from continuing Iran war escalation after the midterms, lifting Exxon and Chevron quarterly earnings. Value beat growth by the most since 2001. Internationally, dollar strength and South Korea/Taiwan tech losses (Samsung, SK Hynix, TSM) plus Brazil's surprise Lula re-election dragged on EM. The piece then turns to the Nov 3 midterms' "Blue Tsunami" Democratic sweep of Congress, citing historical precedent that stocks and the Nasdaq 100 rallied after past midterm-year drawdowns and congressional flips, with the VIX/VXN spread spiking but expected to mean-revert.
